$$
\begin{aligned}({{1-4}_{⏟}}_{-3})^{2}\times \frac{1}{12} & =(-3)^{2}\times \frac{1}{12}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{{(-3)^{2}}_{⏟}}_{9}\times \frac{1}{12} & =9\times \frac{1}{12}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}9\times \frac{1}{12} & = \\ \frac{9}{1}\times \frac{1}{12} & = \\ \frac{9\times 1}{1\times 12} & = \\ \frac{9}{12} & = \\ \frac{9÷3}{12÷3} & = \\ \frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To evaluate this expression, we use PEMDAS. First, consider the expression inside the parenthesis:

$$
\begin{aligned}5÷(-2)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Applying PEMDAS to this expression, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}5÷(-2)^{2} & = \\ 5÷4 & = \\ \frac{5}{4} & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\overset{\frac{5}{4}}{\overset{⏞}{5÷(-2)^{2}}})\times (-\frac{4}{5}) & = \\ \frac{5}{4}\times (-\frac{4}{5}) & = \\ -\frac{5}{4}\times \frac{4}{5} & = \\ -\frac{5\times 4}{4\times 5} & = \\ -\frac{\cancel{5}\times \cancel{4}}{\cancel{4}\times \cancel{5}} & = \\ -1\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
As we already know, to evaluate numerical expressions with a mix of different operations, we must follow the order of operations (PEMDAS).

The same rules apply to numerical expressions with negative numbers. For example, let's compute the value of

$$
(-2) \times (-3)^2.
$$

To evaluate this expression, we use PEMDAS.  First, we compute the exponents:

$$
(-2)\,\times\overbrace{(-3)^2}^{\large\color{blue} 9}  = (-2) \times {\color{blue} 9}
$$

 

Then, we multiply:

$$
(-2) \times 9 = -18
$$

Therefore,

$$
(-2) \times (-3)^2 = -18.
$$
